summary: 1. The Sep 21 Daily Availability Final Report — missed by both the earlier same-day catch-up pass and the continuation pass — is now ingested and compiled. 2. Overall Daily 89.61%, Overall MTD 86.63%, Core Fleet Daily 83.96%, up from Sep 20's 87.03%/86.48%/79.99%. 3. EX-253 stays down the full 24 hours for a sixth consecutive day on its confirmed swing-motor/gearbox fault; DT-128 stays down a fourth consecutive day on the same engine-coolant fault, coincident with the engine swap already logged; DT-106 opens a fresh full-day Tyre Air Pressure Low breakdown; DR-139 closes out the 750-hour service opened Sep 20; EX-123 and EX-263 both open fresh faults right at the report's cutoff. 4. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 2. 5. A dashboard phrasing drift is found across nine days of catch-up entries (Sep 13-21) in two of the three parser-dependent dashboard articles. 6. The daily-production-report.md MTD headline drifted from the required isolated `MTD X BCM (-Y% vs target)` bold span to a differently-shaped, unbolded-fragment sentence, and the crusher-throughput line dropped the word "stockpile"/"sits at." The survey-volume-reconciliation.md MTD gap headline drifted from an isolated `+X BCM (+Y%)` bold span to bolding the entire surrounding sentence, which no longer isolates the figure for a regex match. 7. Both are now restored to the correct isolated-bold form for the current (Sep 21) figures, so the next `wiki-insights-sync` publish run (11:00/17:00) picks up live numbers rather than a stale earlier match. 8. The nine days of already-published Sep 13-21 narrative in between were not rewritten. 9. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[survey-volume-reconciliation]]. 3. With the corrected phrasing in place, the current dashboard figures read: MTD 574,833 BCM (+7.11% vs target); crusher stockpile throughput 43,774.5 LCM against a 124,000 LCM plan (35.30%); survey MTD gap -51,832 BCM (-9.91%), 87.37% of the 598,598 BCM monthly target achieved, 3 days remaining. The Sep 13-21 catch-up-pass paragraphs still carry the drifted phrasing in their own historical text (only the current/latest occurrence was corrected in each article) — a dedicated backfill pass would be needed if Peter wants the historical dashboard-format record clean, though the live dashboard only reads the latest occurrence. EX-123 (Engine Cut Off) and EX-263 (Hydraulic Oil Leaking) both opened fresh faults right at the Sep 21 report's cutoff, in the small hours of Sep 22 — worth checking the Sep 22 Availability Final Report once it lands to see whether either becomes a standing multi-day stoppage the way EX-253 and DT-128 have. DT-106's fresh full-day tyre breakdown lands the same week the Sep 20 shift meeting flagged 92 tyre replacements in 9 months and a pending Gerard pit-severity study — worth cross-referencing once that study reports. See [[safety-inspection-patterns]]. Two "mining-kb-compile" passes ran on the same source material today without coordination (the earlier catch-up/continuation passes, and this follow-up pass), producing a duplicate `_INGESTED.md` registration for `260922-INX-SUM.xlsx` and the Maaden Plans Week 39+40 files. Source: `Maintanance Shedules/Sep 26/DailyAvailability_Final_Report (21-09-2025 ).pdf`. No content removed or renamed from RAW. ---
